section_title: What future can Naomi offer the women she loves?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 6 When Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food, she and her daughters-in-law prepared to leave the land of Moab. 7 Accompanied by her two daughters-in-law, she left the place where she had been living and set out on the road leading back to the land of Judah. 8 Then Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s home. May the LORD show you loving devotion, as you have shown to your dead and to me. 9 May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.” And she kissed them as they wept aloud 10 and said, “Surely we will return with you to your people.”

11 But Naomi replied, “Return home, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb to become your husbands? 12 Return home, my daughters. Go on, for I am too old to have another husband. Even if I thought there was hope for me to have a husband tonight and to bear sons, 13 would you wait for them to grow up? Would you refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, it is much more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.” 14 Again they wept aloud, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.

context_lines: Naomi hears that the LORD has provided food for His people, so she prepares to return to Judah. Orpah and Ruth begin the journey with her. Before they go farther, she urges them to return to their mothers’ homes and seek the security of new marriages.

Her blessing recognizes what they have already given: loving devotion to their husbands and to her. The word is חֶסֶד, *hesed* (KHEH-sed), kindness expressed in faithful care. [Brown–Driver–Briggs](https://biblehub.com/hebrew/2617.htm) describes both human kindness and God’s lovingkindness, specifically listing Naomi’s prayer here. She asks God to show them the care they have shown others.

The women weep and initially insist on accompanying her. Naomi explains that she cannot offer them new husbands from her own household. Even the imagined possibility of having sons would leave them waiting far too long. [Deuteronomy 25:5–10](https://biblehub.com/bsb/deuteronomy/25.htm) gives the background of preserving a deceased brother’s family, but Naomi’s speech shows that no simple solution is available through her.

She describes her own situation as bitter and says the LORD’s hand has gone out against her. Orpah kisses her goodbye, while Ruth clings to her. Naomi’s concern for their future and her sense of personal loss are both present in the conversation.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-book-of-ruth/) and [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ruth/1.htm) understand Naomi’s insistence as requiring the women to consider the cost of going with her. They do not read her as merely indifferent to their welfare or faith. Henry draws attention to her prayer when they face separation; Wesley emphasizes her inability to offer a secure future.

Both also use the two women’s choices as an illustration of differing levels of commitment. They compare a sorrowful departure with a loyalty willing to leave familiar surroundings. The narrative gives Orpah’s farewell and Ruth’s decision here; Ruth’s own explanation of her loyalty follows in the next passage.
god_plan_lines: The kindness Naomi asks for belongs to a theme running through Scripture. In [Exodus 34:5–9](https://biblehub.com/bsb/exodus/34.htm), the LORD declares Himself compassionate and gracious, abundant in loving devotion and faithfulness. Naomi’s prayer seeks care from the God whose character has already been made known to His people.

[Titus 3:3–7](https://biblehub.com/bsb/titus/3.htm) brings God’s kindness into the account of salvation through Jesus. He saves according to mercy, renews by the Holy Spirit, and gives the hope of eternal life. The larger purpose reaches beyond finding immediate security: God’s kindness brings people into a renewed life with Him.
